stem: Which component of a piece of bubble gum does the body not break down?

choices.text: The sweeteners
The gum base
The flavor oils
The softeners

feedback: The gum base is a blend of elastomers, resins, and waxes, and nothing in the digestive tract recognizes it. Sweeteners, flavorings, and softeners all dissolve or leach out during chewing. Re-study block-01 if this was unclear.

stem: Why does a piece of gum that has been chewed for a few minutes blow better than a fresh piece?

choices.text: It has cooled below mouth temperature
It has absorbed saliva and gained mass
Its sugar crystals have dissolved, leaving a smoother film
Its flavor oils have hardened the base

feedback: Undissolved sugar crystals create weak points that a thin film cannot tolerate. Once saliva has carried them off, what remains is base and residual softener, which stretches evenly. Re-study block-02.

stem: In the three-step sequence, what happens immediately before sealing the lips and blowing?

choices.text: The wad is flattened into an even sheet
A pocket is opened with the center of the tongue
The gum is warmed against the roof of the mouth
The flavor oils are allowed to dissipate

feedback: Flattening comes first, then the tongue opens a pocket against the back of the front teeth, and only then do the lips seal. Re-study block-03.

stem: A participant claims that swallowed gum remains in the stomach for years. Which statement best corrects that claim?

choices.text: The base is indigestible but passes through intact within a day or two
The base dissolves slowly over several months
The sweeteners bind the base to the stomach lining
The softeners are digested and the rest is absorbed

feedback: Indigestible is not the same as retained. The base is not broken down, but nothing holds it in place either, so it moves through on the ordinary schedule.

stem: Flavor in a piece of gum fades within a few minutes primarily because

choices.text: body heat degrades the flavor oils
saliva dissolves and carries away the sweeteners and oils
the base absorbs the oils as it softens
the softeners neutralize the oils on contact

feedback: The soluble components leave with saliva. What is left behind is the base and whatever softener has not leached out, which is why the taste goes long before the chew does.

stem: A learner blows hard and fast and consistently gets a hole rather than a bubble. The most likely cause is that

choices.text: the gum was chewed too long before the attempt
the lip seal was too tight for the volume of air
air was forced in faster than the film could stretch
the pocket was opened with the lips rather than the tongue

feedback: The film stretches at a sustainable rate. Exceeding that rate does not produce a larger bubble; it tears the film at whatever point is thinnest.

stem: A bubble deflates slowly without bursting. What does this indicate?

choices.text: The film tore, and the piece should be discarded
The lip seal leaked, and the same piece can be reused
The gum was too fresh and needs further chewing
The pocket was opened too far back on the tongue

feedback: A collapse leaves the film intact, so the failure is at the seal rather than in the gum. A pop is the opposite: the film itself has torn and the attempt cannot be recovered.
